candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-058 — C API limitations prose is stale against its generated inventory
**Severity: low · Confidence: VERIFIED · Area: native C API generated documentation**

The limitations prose reports 6,415 canonical declarations.  The checked-in generated inventory
at the tag partitions **6,712**: 6,317 implemented, 15 partial, zero planned and 380 not
applicable.  The generated data is the reproducible authority; the older prose total is not.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: generated coverage prose and the executable inventory/release gates disagree at TARGET

candidates.title: The alpha.1 C API cannot compile after NanoVG became the 50th renderer identity
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-059 — The alpha.1 C API cannot compile after NanoVG became the 50th renderer identity
**Severity: high · Confidence: REPRODUCED · Area: native C API / renderer registry**

An exact-tag GNU 14.2 build with `CNA_BUILD_C_API=ON`, Net enabled and
HEADLESS/HEADLESS/NULL reaches `modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiCoreExt.cpp:250` and fails its deliberate
static assertion: `RendererIdentities.size()` is 49 while `CanonicalRendererCount()` is 50.
`GraphicsRendererType.hpp` and the canonical registry contain `NanoVg`/`NANOVG`; the C public
constants in `CNA/C/graphics.h` end at `CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER_PIXIJS`, and the mapping table has no
NanoVG row. The same omission explains the stale 49-identity release prose.

This is not a renderer-specific runtime limitation: the adapter translation unit is compiled for
a HEADLESS build and the invariant intentionally covers the complete public identity vocabulary,
so `cna_c_api` cannot be produced in the ordinary configuration. The five dedicated C API
workflows validate generated records but do not build this final target; the source-only aggregate
release checker consequently reports Ready despite the compile failure.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: current C ABI renderer mapping builds against the 25-identity registry

candidates.title: C API plus disabled Net passes configuration and fails on absent GamerServices
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-060 — C API plus disabled Net passes configuration and fails on absent GamerServices
**Severity: medium · Confidence: REPRODUCED · Area: native C API / CMake composition**

`modules/CMakeLists.txt` adds `gamer-services` and `net` only under `CNA_ENABLE_NET`. The C API is
added independently, yet its target unconditionally links `CNA_Net` and `CNA_GamerServices`, and
`CnaCApiDetail.hpp` unconditionally includes GamerServices exception headers. An exact-tag
HEADLESS/HEADLESS/NULL configure with `CNA_BUILD_C_API=ON` and `CNA_ENABLE_NET=OFF` succeeds;
compilation then stops because `GameUpdateRequiredException.hpp` is not on the target's include
path. CMake should either require/force Net for this ABI surface or reject the incompatible tuple
during configuration.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: configuration now rejects C API + disabled networking with an actionable diagnostic

candidates.title: the root runtime-coverage headline is stale after full member closure
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-061 — the root runtime-coverage headline is stale after full member closure
**Severity: medium · Confidence: REPRODUCED · Area: documentation / XNA API audit**

At TARGET, the root `README.md` still presents **3,467 / 3,627** strict documented runtime
members. The checked-in generated audit and its executable checker report **3,627 / 3,627** strict
members and **3,627 / 3,627** C++-applicable members, with 331 / 331 public runtime types. The
headline therefore understates the current representation surface by 160 members and disagrees
with the repository's own generated authority.

This does not imply behavioral parity: the generated report classifies representation and
semantic disposition, while implementation and runtime evidence remain separate layers. The bug
is that the project's highest-visibility summary publishes an obsolete representation count.

**Expected:** regenerate or mechanically source the README headline from the runtime API audit.

**Regression gate:** fail when a live README coverage fraction differs from the generated report.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: root README reports 3,467/3,627 while generated runtime audit proves 3,627/3,627

candidates.title: the C API inventory cannot classify three current public modules
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-062 — the C API inventory cannot classify three current public modules
**Severity: high · Confidence: REPRODUCED · Area: C API release tooling**

Running this command in the detached TARGET tree:

```text
python3 tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py --check
```

exits 2 because `MODULE_SCOPE` says nothing about the existing public include trees for
`modules/design`, `modules/diagnostics`, and `modules/inspector`. The generator deliberately
refuses to let a new module fall through, so this is a valuable failure, but it means the committed
8,363 implemented / 15 partial / 468 planned / 509 not-applicable summary cannot be independently
re-derived at TARGET.

`python3 tools/c-api/check_release_gate.py --run` correspondingly prints both
`coverage-closed` and `limitations-matrix` as **NOT MET** and concludes `NOT READY`, even though
the ABI-baseline criterion still verifies 221 struct layouts and 4,055 exports. This is a tooling
scope defect, not proof that those three modules should all receive C bindings; each needs an
explicit covered/excluded decision.

**Expected:** classify every public module in `MODULE_SCOPE`, regenerate coverage and limitations,
and keep the unknown-module refusal as the regression gate.

---
